newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens higher, but rate worries persist.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens higher, but rate worries persist.

text.p: German shares started bourse trade higher on Wednesday, but volumes were modest and the mood uncertain as worries lingered that the Bundesbank may be poised to raise interest rates to support the ailing deutschemark.
The blue chip DAX index was up 12.76 points at 4,315.07 points a half-hour into the bourse session.
However that level marked a decline from the close of post-bourse electronic dealings on Tuesday, when the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,325.86 points.
Dealers said they were keeping a wary eye on likely interest rate indications, particularly with the dollar trading above 1.88 marks.
"People have become quite unsettled," said a Frankfurt trader. "With the dollar trading at these levels, it seems perfectly probable the Bundesbank will act."
At the same time, the main events of the morning, the release of July jobless data and the Bundesbank's weekly repo tender, appeared to argue against a rate hike.
Germany's seasonally adjusted jobless total rose by an unexpectedly high 17,000 in July, against average forecasts for a rise of 4,000.
Meanwhile the Bundesbank injected a higher-than-expected volume of funds into the market -- adding a net 2.6 billion marks at its weekly tender.
Dealers conceded that these events reduced the chance of a move on rates.
"But this is a risky time. It is not a time to commit yourself to this market," another dealer said.
There was no clear trend or sectoral interest evident among blue chip shares.
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas got an early boost after it reported that its first-half profit jumped to 238 million marks from 184 million marks -- at the top end of forecasts.
The shares hit a high of 223 marks in IBIS trade before settling back to 215.50 marks, down 50 pfennigs in bourse dealings.
